what: Range Resources drills for natural gas in the Marcellus shale of Pennsylvania, and produces a large volume of natural gas liquids such as ethane and propane alongside it.
customers: Gas utilities, power generators, petrochemical plants and export terminals.
money: ethane, propane and butane, much of it exported
moat: Acreage in the liquids-rich part of the Marcellus, where the gas comes with valuable liquids attached, and decades of drilling inventory already held.
risks: Natural gas prices set the revenue and the company has no influence over them
Revenue swung from $5.3B to $2.4B and back to $3.1B in three years
Appalachian pipeline capacity limits how much gas can reach better-paying markets
opportunities: 12.9 times earnings with a 21.1% net margin and $765M of free cash flow
Liquefied natural gas exports and data centre power demand are both new sources of gas demand
Natural gas liquids are priced off oil rather than gas, which diversifies the revenue
watch: Realised gas prices against the benchmark, and the natural gas liquids share of revenue.
